column1: # NUR031 Function-value equality — the second half of the record, after
# the Module-descriptor half (frontier-nur031-module-eq.tsv, resolved
# 2026-08-02). A function's `eq` is REFERENCE identity per NUR011's rule
# for every Ideal, keyed on an identity token minted once per authored
# function and copied by every derivation that leaves it the same
# function; its `deq` is CONTENT equality, compared as canon — which is
# name-independent, so the binding a function was reached through is not
# part of what it is. Before this a function was deq to NOTHING, not even
# itself, which made ADR-015's round-trip unsatisfiable for the kind.
# These rows are semantically GREEN on the interpreter and compile-REFUSED
# on a PRE-EXISTING limitation with nothing to do with equality: a
# function VALUE reaching a non-inert word is refused outright
# ("function value reaches eq/deq/canon (Stage 3)",
# EmitState.RecordCallOperands). The same refusal fires on the pre-fix
# binary for the identical shape — the fix changed the ANSWER, not the
# compile status. Sound interpreter fallback (differential-clean), so the
# ratcheted main corpus does not own them.
# Graduation = a compiled representation for a function value as an
# operand, the Stage-3 fn-value work. At that point delete these ledger
# entries and move the rows into lang/spec/compare-restrict.tsv (the
# NUR031 opaque-Ideal section) and lang/spec/fn-value.tsv.
# --- reflexivity: the defect this record closed --------------------------
def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] f/v eq f/v
column3: a function is reflexively eq — the identity token survives the reach

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] f/v deq f/v
column3: …and reflexively deq, which is what ADR-015's round-trip needs of the kind

column1: # --- eq is reference identity, and identity survives rebinding -----------
def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def a (f/v) def b (f/v) a/v eq b/v
column3: two names for ONE function are eq — identity survives rebinding

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def a (f/v) a/v eq f/v
column3: …and the rebound name is eq to the function it was reached from

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def g fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] f/v eq g/v
column3: GOTCHA: two independently-written functions with identical content are NOT eq — eq is identity, not content

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def g fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] f/v deq g/v
column3: …but they ARE deq: same params, same returns, same body

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def h fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 2] f/v deq h/v
column3: a different BODY is a different value — deq discriminates it

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def s fn x:String [String] [x] f/v deq s/v
# --- content is canon, and canon carries no binding name -----------------
def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] canon (f/v)
column3: canon renders the anonymous fn literal — no `fn f`, because the name is how it was reached

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] def a (f/v) (canon (a/v)) eq (canon (f/v))
column3: so one function under two names has ONE canon — the name-independence deq rides on

column1: # --- cross-kind: a function against a non-function -----------------------
def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] f/v eq 1
column3: cross-type eq is false, never an error

column1: def f fn x:Integer [Integer] [x add 1] f/v deq 1
# --- the record's measurable acceptance signal ---------------------------
# A namespace is deq-reflexive only when every export is. A module
# exporting a FUNCTION was therefore not deq to itself — the fn
# fall-through seen through a namespace, and the signal the verdict named
# for this record.
import "boru:io" IO deq IO
column3: a function-exporting namespace is deq to itself — the fn fall-through, closed

column1: import "boru:string-util" StringUtil deq StringUtil
column3: …and so is every other native module's namespace
